name: schroedinger
desc: High-speed implementation of the Dirac codec
why: A high-speed Dirac wavelet codec, an obscure and historic video format implementation worth decoding by hand.

brief.what_it_is: Schroedinger is a C/C++ library implementing the Dirac video codec, a wavelet-based format originally created by the BBC Research department. Per its Launchpad page, it is meant for user applications, in contrast to dirac-research, the Dirac project's research encoder. The page describes it as a Dirac video codec and says it outperforms dirac-research in most encoding situations on speed and visual quality. The page does not describe its inputs or outputs, or any command-line tool.
brief.why_it_exists: The Dirac project maintains two encoders: dirac-research, a research encoder, and Schroedinger, meant for user applications. Schroedinger exists to be the faster, practical Dirac implementation.
brief.install_notes: The Launchpad page links a 1.0.11 source tarball (schroedinger...0.11.tar.gz, released 2012-01-23) and an 'All downloads' page. Distribution packages exist in Ubuntu (Xenial 1.0.11-2.1build1, Trusty, Precise, Wheezy, Squeeze). The page gives no build steps, dependencies, or first-run instructions. The source is in Bazaar (lp:schroedinger), and the page also shows a git-style hash, 56f1eb7, in its footer.
brief.standout: Its name is a nod to Erwin Schrödinger, who shared the 1933 Nobel Prize with Paul Dirac, the namesake of the Dirac codec. The codec is a historic wavelet-based video format that was built by the BBC and later taken up by a wider open-source group.
brief.status: Quiet. The latest release is 1.0.11 from 2012-01-23, the Launchpad project was registered 2013-06-08, and the most recent distro package upload seen is 2014-12-16 (Xenial). The page says the trunk series is the current focus of development, but no recent trunk activity is visible on the page.
brief.caveats: The homepage gives no platform list, build instructions, or dependencies. The package is a library and the Homebrew formula lists no executables, so it may not be useful on its own without a host program. The page lists several licences, including GPL v2/v3, LGPL v2.1/v3, MIT/X, and MPL, so check the source tree before reusing code. The Launchpad page is the only source read here, and the scout note's suggestion of decoding by hand is not supported by anything on the page.
quotes: Schrödinger is a Dirac video codec meant for user applications.
Schrödinger outperforms dirac-research in most encoding situations, both in terms of encoding speed and visual quality.

Originally created by the BBC Research department, the Dirac project has expanded to include companies providing hardware equipment and software for handling Dirac video, as well as an active open-source development group.
